title: OXO Brew Compact Conical Burr Electric Coffee Bean Grinder - 50g Capacity | Countertop Coffee Grinder, Consistent Grind Size, Multiple Settings, Home Brew, Stainless Steel

reviews.title: I really, really like this grinder.
reviews.body: Before buying this I read the reviews complaining about noise, mess and complexity. It was with some trepidation, then, that I placed the order.I've had noisy grinders. One famous make is loud enough that I routinely left the room while it ran. This OXO grinder is not noisy by any stretch, running at a low growl even without being placed on a towel to buffer the vibration.As to mess and complexity, operation is simple and foolproof. Put beans in the top. Press the button. When it stops grinding, twist the top to remove the grinder assembly and, lo, there rests the ground coffee with (hopefully) all the aroma you put into roasting.I'll admit to adopting some degree of preparation. It requires a cereal bowl, a spoon and a coffee filter. When the grind is complete, twist and remove the grinder (top portion) assembly and place it with burr down on the open coffee filter. Tilt and pour the grounds into the cereal bowl. Reassemble the grinder. Place the filter in the coffee machine and measure the coffee into the filter with the spoon. Any extra coffee is placed in a waiting grounds jar.Yes, it's mind-boggling in its complexity.Often one or two specks escape and hide on the counter top. My wife offered to assist if I'm unable to deal with it. Usually while rinsing the bowl and spoon. I know, extra work.I've had less static buildup and messy operation with OXO than with more famous grinders that take up twice the counter space, howl like a banshee and explode their grounds across the kitchen. In contrast, this is solid, relatively quiet, and radiates durability in the look and feel. I'm very pleased with it.

reviews.title: Elite Grinder!
reviews.body: Awesome Burr grinder! I got a new espresso machine and my blade grinder was not able to uniformily do espresso fine grind. This does it easily and you can grind as much or as little as needed into the included hopper! I found a "fine 2/3" setting works well for my espresso. But you can adjust to yr liking for french press, drip etc. The time selection just caculates how much you want it to grind. Start on 10 seconds for single use & more time if you want to fill a canister. It has a slim profile and does not take up a lot of counter space. About as tall as paper towels & included pics for reference. Easy to use, nice looking, no mess, not loud and love having fresh ground coffee, so easy!  Great for households with different coffee preps too. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Consistent Grind Made a Noticeable Difference. Worth the Upgrade From Blade Grinding
reviews.body: Switched over from a cheap blade grinder after our pour over kept coming out inconsistent, some sips watery and some over extracted depending on which chunks of bean happened to get pulverized versus barely chopped. Wanted actual conical burrs instead of blades chopping randomly.Grind consistency has been the biggest improvement, coffee tastes noticeably more even cup to cup now, no more guessing why one morning's brew tasted off compared to the day before. Range of grind settings covers everything from a coarse french press to fine enough for pour over, haven't found a setting yet that felt like it was missing for what we brew at home.12 oz capacity holds plenty for our household's weekly bean supply without needing to refill mid grind, and the hopper is easy to see through to check how much is left. Grinding itself is relatively quiet compared to what I braced for based on some reviews of similar grinders, doesn't wake anyone up grinding early before work.Cleanup is straightforward too, removable burr assembly and everything wipes out easy without oily bean residue building up somewhere hard to reach. For the price, this got us proper burr grinding without paying for some of the pricier standalone grinder brands that do the same basic job, real value for a home setup that just wants consistent coffee. Only complaint is it's a little louder then expected right when it starts up before settling into a steadier grind sound. Great upgrade from blade grinding, would buy again.

reviews.title: Great grinder
reviews.body: It's been a great grinder so far. Only had it a few days, so I can't say much about it's durability, but it seems pretty solid. It grinds much better than my old spice grinder and my coffee grounds come out pretty consistent. It's definitely helped improve my regular coffee and cold brew coffee as well. The cold brew especially. It's pretty fast at grinding enough coffee grounds for a full carafe. Takes about 25-30 seconds on average for me. It's not the easiest thing to clean, but it comes apart easily enough to clean the insides with a brush. My only gripe with it is that it's a bit louder than my spice grinder. It's not horribly loud like some reviews said, but it's definitely not quiet either. Definitely don't use early in the morning if you have any light sleepers in the house. While it's definitely on the pricey side, I'd definitely recommend it if you want a good grinder or do a ton of cold brew coffee.

reviews.title: Best single serving grinder!
reviews.body: This grinder is fantastic.The reviews that talk about the grinder arriving used? Ignore them. When you get the box, it states they test their grinders with a small amount of coffee beans before packaging and may be residual coffee bean in the grinder.Complaints about static? Thats normal for grinders. Some grinders handle static better than others, but in simple terms, when you grind the beans at a high speed, you are actually stripping electrons which creates a charge imbalance, thus you have static. THANKFULLY they include a mini glass water spray bottle in the box. Spray your beans in the top hopper 3-4 times before grinding, shake em a little bit, then grind. This should drastically minimize the static in most cases.The footprint of this machine is what made it so attractive to me. It's truly compact and serves all of my coffee needs. You dont really need a hopper bigger than this 50g for at home use. You should be grinding your beans fresh every time you brew anyways. Only time I need more than 50g of bean at a time is if im making multiple cups for multiple people or if I'm making cold brew. It's so easy to use though, that running through a 2nd hopper of beans is such a none issue.Extremely easy to take apart and clean. Quieter than my last machine I bought 5 years ago. Grounds are consistent enough is size across grind sizes.Just PLEASE read the manual and the notices on the box. So many complaints I read that made me hesitant in buying this were explained literally on the box. The moment I opened it, read everything and tested, I fell in love with the machine.

Furthermore, my wife has been in contact via email with OXO's customer support team about the poor quality of this product, and their support team refuses to either refund or replace the product.  We have provided them with both videos and photos showing that the unit functions either very poorly or does not function at all without lots of troubleshooting.  Yet, their engineers have responded saying that the unit appears to be functioning "normally" in the videos (one of which I will attach to this review).  However, at this point the unit does not work without quite a bit of frustration--plugging and unplugging multiple times or sweeping out the burrs multiple times just to grind enough beans for a pour over coffee.  Even though I have only owned this unit for one month, I see no other solution than to place this unit in the trash and buy a more expensive unit from another manufacturer.  I am an avid home coffee brewer, and I have owned other coffee products from Bonavita, Hario, Mr. Coffee, Cuisinart, and OXO.  I can say unequivocally, this OXO burr grinder is the worst coffee product I have ever owned or purchased.  I will attach video and photographic proof that the unit does not work correctly and will explain further below the problems with the unit.Initially, the unit worked great.  For the first week, the unit produced a reliable and consistent grind of Trader Joe's Ethiopian beans (~$8.99 a bag).  Then, the trouble started the second week when I began grinding Stumptown Hair Bender beans (~$15.99 a bag).  The unit jammed mid-cycle for the first time.  The button on the front of the unit would not start the motor so I tried troubleshooting the unit in multiple ways, following the instructions in the owner's manual.  I unplugged it and plugged it back in--start button still did not work.  I opened the bean hopper and nothing appeared jammed.  So finally I opened up the burrs and swept them out.  When I put the unit back together, it worked, and I thought the problem was solved.  However, over the next week, the unit kept jamming every time I used it with the Stumptown beans.  Sometimes it would jam multiple times in a row.  Each time I had to open the unit and sweep out the burrs to get it to work.  This process, while being extremely frustrating and time-consuming, also caused the unit to produce an inconsistent grind size.  I've attached a picture showing that I get chunks of beans in my pour over because I have to play an elaborate game with the machine just to get it to function.  For a unit that regularly retails for around $100, this is absolutely unacceptable for a new product.  Furthermore, if a $100 burr grinder cannot be used on a premium product like Stumptown, then that grinder is entirely worthless to coffee enthusiasts.After I finished the bag of Stumptown coffee, I tried the grinder again on the Trader Joe's beans (since those beans had initially worked well with the unit).  Now, I began experiencing the same problems with Trader Joe's.  In order to grind 5 scoops of beans for one large pour over coffee, I had to either: (1) Open and sweep the burrs multiple times or (2) Plug and unplug the unit multiple times because it grinds for about 3 seconds before jamming even when the timer is set on 30 seconds.  I have attached a video showing the unit functioning in this way.  In the video, you will see the game I have to play just to grind beans using a unit that was purchased only 3 weeks prior.Here's my personal thought regarding the performance issues of the machine.  I assume the motor has a fail-safe feature designed to stop the motor in event that it becomes clogged.  This would prevent the motor from being damaged if a very small stone or an extremely hard bean got stuck in the burrs (which can happen on a rare occasion).  My guess is that this setting isn't quite right in my unit and that the unit stops every time there is the tiniest bit of resistance on the motor.  This would explain why I have to unplug the unit multiple times just to completely grind a cup of beans.  Either way, it is entirely unreasonable for OXO to expect users to have to troubleshoot a new unit with such frequency as a part of the unit's "normal" functioning.Currently, OXO does not want to address my concerns with this unit so I have decided to place this negative review.  I've never felt compelled before to write a negative review on Amazon.  Hopefully, they will decide to improve the product and respond to customer concerns.  At this point, I cannot recommend this product to any other buyer, and I will no longer purchase any kitchen or coffee products manufactured by OXO.  Finally, I've decided I don't even want a replacement for this unit.  Even if OXO offered to replace it, I would refuse.  That alone shows my level of disappointment with the product.  The overall build quality feels cheap to me, especially the timer and start button on the front.  I owned an entry-level Mr. Coffee burr grinder (~$30) for 7 years that "felt" better--button quality, weight of product, sound of motor, etc.  If OXO decides to respond to my concerns, I will only accept a full refund for the purchase price of the product so that I can purchase another unit from a different manufacturer.UPDATE: OXO finally agreed to refund us the purchase price of the unit after I posted this negative review and video on Amazon.  The refund process took some time, but we did eventually get a check in the mail for the full purchase price of the unit.  We will explore other options for a replacement unit.

reviews.title: This is a GREAT Coffee Grinder!
reviews.body: I have had quite a few coffee grinders in my day.  Most of them were those little oval Krups blade grinders.  I also got a Krups burr grinder, but it wasn't very good and didn't last very long.  But this Oxo Conical Burr Coffee Grinder is several cuts above.  It takes a little bit of experimenting to get the coarseness and amount just right, but once you do it is consistent and does not result in any residual fine dust.  Its steel cup is nice and the coffee doesn't stick to it, and its reservoir, with a mouth large enough to simply dump the beans into it right out of the bag without bothering with any scooper, holds enough coffee for about five days at 8 good medium-strength cups/day.  You just push the button, release it, and voila!  And, for a coffee grinder, it is rather quiet.  So consistent, so easy to use, such good coffee!  I HIGHLY recommend it.
